search_log: Searched "Nicholas Sparks The Rescue excerpt first chapter publisher" and opened the author-hosted PDF, Google Books record, BookBrowse excerpt, and permissioned ReadingGroupGuides excerpt.

Searched "The Rescue Nicholas Sparks point of view third person narrator" and exact variants including Denise and Taylor; no authoritative source explicitly labeled the whole novel's grammatical person.
Searched for epistolary, frame-narrative, multiple-narrator, and alternating-point-of-view descriptions; found no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person sections.
Opened the Los Angeles Times contemporary review; it discusses the novel's access to both protagonists' viewpoints and supplies third-person interior quotations.
Checked Google Books and Nicholas Sparks's writing notes; they verified the work and structure but did not directly describe narrative person.
Searched the exact q00536 distance quotation and its longer Goodreads variant; results did not establish it as controlling narration, and the longer form is aphoristic and dialogue-like.
person_note: The base narration is third person, with focalization through both Denise and Taylor. Several interior Goodreads passages expose a nonparticipating narrator reporting their private thoughts, and the authorized opening sustains the same form. First- and second-person forms in the quote set are overwhelmingly dialogue or gnomic address; q00536 is an isolated aphoristic first-person fragment and is treated as a local/clipped voice rather than evidence of a first-person section. No researched source indicated an epistolary frame or sustained change of grammatical person. Confidence is medium because the strongest authorized prose evidence is limited to the opening, although interior quotes and the full-book review corroborate the classification.
